The dashboard takes the json's `ran_at` unconditionally whenever the json exists — including when the json is older than the tracked record. E.g., a developer with a stale local `audit-report.json` (from a run before pulling a newer tracked `last_audit` record) will see the dashboard regress to an older date than the tracked record. The spec fixes "md older than json"; this is the mirror case and it's not guarded or tested.
findings.suggestion: Only override when `_instant(ran) >= _instant(freshness.latest.ran_at)`, or at least pin the current behavior (older json wins) in a test so it's a deliberate choice.

findings.finding: When `latest_full.ran_at == latest.ran_at`, `full` is replaced with the re-dated `latest` — but `latest` and `latest_full` are different records (scope/checks differ). Re-dating `latest` also keeps its other fields (e.g. whatever `format_note`/`_checks_sentence` print) un-rebased on the new date, so a partially-updated record could render internally inconsistent output. When the ran_ats differ, only `latest` is re-dated and `full` keeps the old instant, so the dashboard can then cite two runs in one section.
findings.suggestion: Either re-date both consistently or leave `full` untouched; add a test with a `latest_full` whose `ran_at` differs to pin the intended behavior.

findings.finding: The record path is wrapped in a broad `except Exception` that converts any failure into `recorded: False`. If `record_audit_run` rejects `ran_at` (or any future signature drift), the run completes "green" while the durable record silently keeps the old date — exactly the divergence this change exists to prevent. The tests confirm the signature works today, so this is only a fragility note, not a live defect.
findings.suggestion: Narrow the swallow (or at least surface `recorded: False` loudly, e.g. stderr) so a divergence between json and record is visible rather than silent.  Positive notes: the tests are behavior-pinning (they assert the rendered date strings, the stale banner text, and the fallback path), not just call-count checks; `_instant` correctly handles both `Generated: ... UTC` stamps and ISO `ran_at`; the "unparseable Generated → stale, date unknown" degradation is tested. The core acceptance criteria (md/json/dashboard agree on a fixture; stale md can't silently show an older date; tests pin it) appear satisfied.  Overall assessment: sound implementation with behavior-driven tests; the findings are edge cases worth a guard or a pinning test, but nothing blocks. Ship with the low-severity hardening.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve

findings.finding: The Markdown renderer uses the in-memory timestamp, and a JSON-only write leaves the existing Markdown on disk with its old `Generated:` date. The stale-report test only gets a warning by calling `mark_audit_report_stale()` separately, so it misses the inconsistent state immediately after the write.
findings.suggestion: Make the JSON record authoritative when rendering the last-run date. On a JSON-only write, automatically mark any existing Markdown as historical and show the current recorded date alongside it. Test the state immediately after the write.

findings.finding: A valid `audit-report.json` contributes no last-run date if the tracked record is missing or invalid. The dashboard can therefore omit a run that the JSON and Markdown both document.
findings.suggestion: Display the JSON last-run date independently of tracked-record validity. Add a fixture with a valid JSON report and no tracked record.

findings.finding: Replacing only the tracked run’s timestamp can attach old results to a different run. If the tracked record describes a June full audit and July’s JSON comes from a partial audit, the dashboard presents June’s results as a July full audit. The lagging-record test checks dates alone and passes with this misattribution.
findings.suggestion: Keep each run’s timestamp, scope, and results together. Add a regression test with an older tracked full audit and a newer partial JSON report, and assert that each retains its own date and scope.

findings.finding: A normal run can flag its own Markdown as older. JSON preserves microseconds, while `Generated:` truncates to seconds, so the strict comparison treats two representations of the same run as different instants. The current-report fixture uses a whole-second timestamp and misses this.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the exact run timestamp in Markdown metadata and use it for comparison. For legacy reports, compare at the precision of the displayed stamp. Add a fixture with a fractional-second timestamp.  Overall assessment: Ship-with-fixes. The shared timestamp works when both reports are written together, but JSON-only updates and mismatched records can still produce stale dates or misattribute audit results.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
